items.title:
RT by @balajis: Balaji Srinivasan on taking the L to set up for the W:

"Before Satya Nadella took over Microsoft, it was losing on mobile to iOS and Android."

"He took the L... and he said, 'You know what? Linux is there. Linux is not going to go away.'"

"We're going to run Linux on Microsoft hardware."

"Mobile is not going away and nobody's installing the Microsoft mobile OS."

"So we're going to allow Word and PowerPoint and Excel to run on iOS and Android devices."

"And... the browser isn't going away. So we're going to make Office 365 work in the cloud."

"Because he took the L, Satya set Microsoft up for the W."

@balajis with @PeterMcCormack

items.title_zh:
RT by @balajis：Balaji Srinivasan 谈从 L 方向准备 W 方向：

“在萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 接管微软之前，微软在移动领域输给了 iOS 和 Android。”

“他拿了 L...然后他说，‘你知道吗？Linux 就在那里。Linux 不会消失。’”

“我们将在微软硬件上运行Linux。”

“移动不会消失，没有人会安装微软移动操作系统。”

“因此，我们将允许 Word、PowerPoint 和 Excel 在 iOS 和 Android 设备上运行。”

“而且......浏览器不会消失。因此我们将使 Office 365 在云中工作。”

“因为 Satya 选了 L，所以他把 Microsoft 设置为 W。”

@balajis 和 @PeterMcCormack
items.title_bilingual:
RT by @balajis：Balaji Srinivasan 谈从 L 方向准备 W 方向：

“在萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 接管微软之前，微软在移动领域输给了 iOS 和 Android。”

“他拿了 L...然后他说，‘你知道吗？Linux 就在那里。Linux 不会消失。’”

“我们将在微软硬件上运行Linux。”

“移动不会消失，没有人会安装微软移动操作系统。”

“因此，我们将允许 Word、PowerPoint 和 Excel 在 iOS 和 Android 设备上运行。”

“而且......浏览器不会消失。因此我们将使 Office 365 在云中工作。”

“因为 Satya 选了 L，所以他把 Microsoft 设置为 W。”

@balajis 和 @PeterMcCormack / RT by @balajis: Balaji Srinivasan on taking the L to set up for the W:

"Before Satya Nadella took over Microsoft, it was losing on mobile to iOS and Android."

"He took the L... and he said, 'You know what? Linux is there. Linux is not going to go away.'"

"We're going to run Linux on Microsoft hardware."

"Mobile is not going away and nobody's installing the Microsoft mobile OS."

"So we're going to allow Word and PowerPoint and Excel to run on iOS and Android devices."

"And... the browser isn't going away. So we're going to make Office 365 work in the cloud."

"Because he took the L, Satya set Microsoft up for the W."

@balajis with @PeterMcCormack

items.title:
R to @balajis: Btw: this isn't meant to be a dunk on @phl43, as I know what he meant. He's saying the (inherited) logistics infrastructure of the US is so impressive that it can seemingly wage endless wars overseas without any impact on the homefront.

And that has indeed been the case in the past. Iraq, Afghanistan, Syria, Libya...all were essentially watched on a TV screen without much impact on daily life within the US.

However, the head of the International Energy Agency has said this is the largest disruption in history. Larger than 1973, which did indeed have a huge impact on daily life in America, though that's before the time of most of those now living.

Is today's America truly in better shape than it was in 1973, in terms of manufacturing might, social homogeneity, and the like? Will it truly be untouched by this global energy crisis? I guess we will find out.
https://archive.is/LYg59

items.title_zh:
R 致@balajis：顺便说一句：这并不意味着@phl43 上的扣篮，因为我知道他的意思。他说，美国（继承的）后勤基础设施令人印象深刻，以至于它似乎可以在海外发动无休止的战争，而不会对国内产生任何影响。

过去确实如此。伊拉克、阿富汗、叙利亚、利比亚……基本上都是在电视屏幕上观看的，对美国的日常生活没有太大影响。

然而，国际能源署署长表示，这是历史上最大的破坏。比 1973 年更大，这确实对美国的日常生活产生了巨大影响，尽管那是在大多数现在生活的人的时代之前。

今天的美国在制造业实力、社会同质性等方面真的比 1973 年更好吗？它真的不会受到这场全球能源危机的影响吗？我想我们会找到答案的。
https://archive.is/LYg59

This is the wrong way of thinking about it.

By this logic, a school shooter is "powerful" because they can kill an entire school.

Real power is the power to build, to maintain stability and prosperity.

It's not the power to destroy. Anyone can kill. Anyone can bomb, destabilize, spread chaos, set fires, create anarchy. Unfortunately, that's relatively easy.

The old America could build, not just kill.
That's the America I admire.
